proofs.proof_tex:
Fix an arbitrary represented model \(\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\) and assignments \(x\), \(c\), and \(y\) in their declared discrete support spaces.  For every \(A\subseteq V\), put
\[
 \mathcal X_A(\mathbf M)
 :=\prod_{v\in A}\operatorname{supp}_{\mathbf M}(V_v),
\]
with \(\mathcal X_{\varnothing}(\mathbf M)\) equal to the singleton containing the empty assignment.  Each coordinate support is at most countable because the model is discrete, and \(V\) is finite by the definitions of \(V\) and \(n\).  Hence every \(\mathcal X_A(\mathbf M)\), in particular \(\mathcal X_Y(\mathbf M)\), is at most countable.  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}disjoint\text{-}query\text{-}sets}\) makes the assignment \(a\in\mathcal X_W(\mathbf M)\), defined by \(a_X=x\) and \(a_C=c\), well defined.  At a role state \(\rho=(\bar X,\bar C)\), write \(\bar x=a_{\bar X}\) and \(\bar c=a_{\bar C}\), and define the proof-local conditional kernel
\[
 K_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y)
 :=P_{\mathbf M}\!\left(
 Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x),
 \bar C=\bar c,S=\mathbf 1\right).
 \tag{1}
\]
The sets in (1) are pairwise compatible: the definition of a role state gives \(\bar X\mathbin{\dot\cup}\bar C=W=X\cup C\), while \(Y\cap W=\varnothing\) follows from \(\mathrm{ass{:}disjoint\text{-}query\text{-}sets}\).  By \(\mathrm{ass{:}positive\text{-}discrete\text{-}selected\text{-}model}\), the selected conditioning stratum used in (1) has positive mass at every assignment under consideration; explicitly,
\[
 P_{\mathbf M}\!\left(
 \bar C=\bar c,S=\mathbf 1
 \mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x)\right)>0.
 \tag{2}
\]
In particular, \(P_{\mathbf M}(S=\mathbf 1\mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x))\) is at least the quantity in (2) and is positive.  Thus every conditional probability and every division below is defined, including the boundary case \(\bar C=\varnothing\).

We first prove invariance along the role-state graph.  At its root \(\rho_0=(X,C)\), Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}target\text{-}query}\) gives
\[
 K_{\rho_0,\mathbf M}(y)
 =P_{\mathbf M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x),C=c,S=\mathbf 1)
 =\psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c).
 \tag{3}
\]
Consider an edge that moves a nonempty current bucket intersection \(T\subseteq\bar X\) from treatment to conditioning.  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}reachable\text{-}role\text{-}graph}\) includes this edge only when the corresponding Rule--2 separation holds.  Apply \(\mathrm{lem{:}selected\text{-}rule\text{-}two}\) with
\[
 A_0=Y,\qquad B_0=T,\qquad C_0=\bar C,
 \qquad D_0=\bar X\setminus T.
\]
These four sets are pairwise disjoint by the role partition and \(Y\cap W=\varnothing\).  Using the restrictions of \(a\) on both sides of the Rule--2 equality yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 K_{(\bar X,\bar C),\mathbf M}(y)
 &=P_{\mathbf M}\!\left(
 Y=y\mid \bar C=\bar c,
 \operatorname{do}(T=a_T,\bar X\setminus T=a_{\bar X\setminus T}),
 S=\mathbf 1\right)\\
 &=P_{\mathbf M}\!\left(
 Y=y\mid T=a_T,\bar C=\bar c,
 \operatorname{do}(\bar X\setminus T=a_{\bar X\setminus T}),
 S=\mathbf 1\right)\\
 &=K_{(\bar X\setminus T,\,\bar C\cup T),\mathbf M}(y).
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
If instead an edge moves a nonempty \(T\subseteq\bar C\) from conditioning to treatment, apply the same lemma with
\[
 A_0=Y,\qquad B_0=T,\qquad C_0=\bar C\setminus T,
 \qquad D_0=\bar X.
\]
Reading its equality from right to left gives
\[
 K_{(\bar X,\bar C),\mathbf M}(y)
 =K_{(\bar X\cup T,\,\bar C\setminus T),\mathbf M}(y).
 \tag{5}
\]
Induction on the length of any directed trace from \(\rho_0\), using (3)--(5), proves
\[
 K_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y)=\psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c)
 \quad\text{for every reachable role state }\rho.
 \tag{6}
\]

Suppose now that Branch-sCIDP succeeds at \(\rho=(\bar X,\bar C)\).  Its terminal sIDP call has outcome set \(A_0=Y\cup\bar C\) and intervention set \(B_0=\bar X\).  They are disjoint, and \(A_0\neq\varnothing\) by \(\mathrm{ass{:}nonempty\text{-}outcome}\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}sidp\text{-}soundness}\), applied directly on the published positive discrete class \(\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\), therefore gives, pointwise for every \(y'\in\mathcal X_Y(\mathbf M)\),
\[
 F_\rho(y',\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})
 =J_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y',\bar c;\bar x).
 \tag{7}
\]
This is not an inference from the rational binary certificate subclass.  The events indexed by \(y'\in\mathcal X_Y(\mathbf M)\) are disjoint and exhaust the outcome assignment space.  That space is at most countable, as shown above, and the summands in (7) are nonnegative point masses.  Countable additivity of the selected interventional probability measure and the definition of \(D_{\rho,\mathbf M}\) therefore give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sum_{y'\in\mathcal X_Y(\mathbf M)}
 F_\rho(y',\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})
 &=\sum_{y'\in\mathcal X_Y(\mathbf M)}
 J_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y',\bar c;\bar x)\\
 &=P_{\mathbf M}\!\left(
 \bar C=\bar c\mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x),S=\mathbf 1\right)\\
 &=D_{\rho,\mathbf M}(\bar c;\bar x)>0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
The last inequality follows from (2) and the positivity of the selected-intervention normalizer established immediately after (2).  Dividing (7) by (8), applying the definition of conditional probability, and then applying (6), we obtain
\[
 \frac{F_\rho(y,\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})}
 {\sum_{y'\in\mathcal X_Y(\mathbf M)}
 F_\rho(y',\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})}
 =K_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y)
 =\psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c).
 \tag{9}
\]
Thus the normalized returned expression is an observed-law identifying map for the causal target.  Its equality with the target has been derived from Rule--2 invariance, countable additivity, positivity, and sIDP soundness, rather than imposed by definition.

It remains to prove the graph-search and cache bounds.  A role state is uniquely determined by \(\bar X\subseteq W\), since \(\bar C=W\setminus\bar X\).  Hence
\[
 |\Omega(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)|\leq 2^{|W|}=2^{|X\cup C|}.
 \tag{10}
\]
A trace with no repeated state and \(r\) visited states has \(r-1\) edges, so (10) gives the asserted upper bound \(2^{|X\cup C|}-1\) on its length.

At each visited state, the outer enumeration tests at most two directions for each of at most \(n\) buckets.  Each relevant manipulated graph has polynomial size in \(n\).  A Rule--2 separation test is decided by a finite reachability search over its admissible edge-incidence states; bucket formation, anterior closure, and region formation are also graph searches of polynomial size.  Consequently all outer role-state work is
\[
 O\!\left(2^n\operatorname{poly}(n)\right).
 \tag{11}
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem{:}sidp\text{-}recursion\text{-}structure}\), a deterministic BuildTree subproblem is keyed by one region \(R\subseteq V\), and a fixing subproblem is keyed by one pair \(R\subseteq T_0\subseteq V\).  There are \(2^n\) keys of the first kind and
\[
 \#\{(R,T_0):R\subseteq T_0\subseteq V\}
 =\sum_{T_0\subseteq V}2^{|T_0|}
 =(1+2)^n=3^n
 \tag{12}
\]
keys of the second kind.  The last equality follows directly by assigning each vertex independently to \(R\), to \(T_0\setminus R\), or to \(V\setminus T_0\).  The same recursion lemma states that BuildTree descends only to proper region children and that every successful fixing iteration removes a nonempty bucket.  Therefore each deterministic key terminates.  Under Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}shared\text{-}formula\text{-}cache}\), it is evaluated at most once and incurs only \(\operatorname{poly}(n)\) graph work.  Equations (11) and (12) thus bound all cached graph computation by
\[
 O\!\left(3^n\operatorname{poly}(n)\right).
 \tag{13}
\]
Each product, quotient, and assembly operation contributes a constant-arity node to the shared formula DAG.  A marginalization over a discrete support is represented by one symbolic summation-binder node whose body and support expression point to cached nodes; it is not expanded into one node per support point.  Thus allowing an at most countable discrete support does not change the graph-search count in (13).  Constructing and emitting all formula nodes, including each such discrete-support summation binder, costs \(O(L_{\mathrm{form}})\) by the definition of \(L_{\mathrm{form}}\).  Combining this output cost with (13) proves
\[
 O\!\left(3^n\operatorname{poly}(n)+L_{\mathrm{form}}\right).
\]
The proof invoked sIDP soundness only after a terminal call succeeded.  It therefore gives no implication from \(\operatorname{AllFail}\) to nonidentification, exactly as claimed.

Assume \(S=\varnothing\).  The selection event is then the sure event, so Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}target\text{-}query}\) reduces to
\[
 \psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c)
 =P_{\mathbf M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x),C=c).
 \tag{1}
\]
In this specialization, \(\mathrm{lem{:}selected\text{-}rule\text{-}two}\) is the ordinary PAG Rule--2 equality because no selection coordinate occurs on either side.

Suppose first that CIDP succeeds.  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}cidp\text{-}no\text{-}selection\text{-}contract}\), it performs a finite sequence of legal Rule--2 moves of nonempty intersections with current buckets, reaches a role state \(\rho_\star=(\bar X_\star,\bar C_\star)\), and identifies the joint kernel
\[
 P_{\mathbf M}\!\left(
 Y,\bar C_\star\mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X_\star)
 \right).
 \tag{2}
\]
Every move in this sequence satisfies exactly the edge condition in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}reachable\text{-}role\text{-}graph}\).  Hence \(\rho_\star\in\Omega(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)\), and Branch-sCIDP visits it unless an earlier terminal call succeeds.  If sIDP returned \(\operatorname{Fail}\) at \(\rho_\star\), Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}sidp\text{-}completeness}\) would imply that the joint kernel (2) is not identified over the represented model class.  This contradicts the identification of (2) supplied by the CIDP contract.  Therefore sIDP succeeds at \(\rho_\star\), or Branch-sCIDP has already succeeded at an earlier visited state.  Thus CIDP success implies Branch-sCIDP success.

Conversely, suppose Branch-sCIDP succeeds.  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}branch\text{-}soundness}\) supplies an observed-law functional equal, throughout the represented positive discrete class, to the right-hand side of (1).  The conditional causal query is therefore identified.  Completeness in \(\mathrm{lem{:}cidp\text{-}no\text{-}selection\text{-}contract}\) rules out CIDP failure, so CIDP succeeds.  This proves agreement of the two identification decisions.

For the formula claim, let \(\Phi_{\mathrm B}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) denote any normalized functional returned by a successful Branch-sCIDP state, and let \(\Phi_{\mathrm C}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) denote the normalized joint functional returned by CIDP.  Branch soundness and the soundness clause of \(\mathrm{lem{:}cidp\text{-}no\text{-}selection\text{-}contract}\), respectively, imply that for every compatible positive discrete model \(\mathbf M\),
\[
 \Phi_{\mathrm B}(P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})
 =P_{\mathbf M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x),C=c)
 =\Phi_{\mathrm C}(P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M}).
 \tag{3}
\]
Both normalizations are defined because the positive discrete model assumption makes their conditioning denominators positive; discrete marginalization, interpreted by countable additivity when a support is countably infinite, also covers the boundary cases \(C=\varnothing\) and an empty terminal conditioning role.  Equation (3) is precisely pointwise equality of the two functionals on the observational-law domain represented by \(\mathcal P\).  Hence every successful Branch-sCIDP formula is equal pointwise on that domain to a CIDP identifying functional.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: When \(S=\varnothing\), Branch-sCIDP and CIDP agree on the identification decision for \(P_{\mathbf M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x),C=c)\), and every successful Branch-sCIDP formula is equal pointwise on the represented observational-law domain to a CIDP identifying functional.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original wording can overstate a syntactic relationship between distinct symbolic expressions. Soundness of both procedures proves the exact invariant needed here: equality at every represented observational law.

prose_updates.honest_scope: No selected conditional completeness theorem is claimed. Branch-sCIDP soundness is stated over the published positive discrete class and allows countable discrete coordinate supports; because the observed vertex set is finite, every joint outcome assignment space used in normalization is at most countable. The affine compiler and the explicit tabular witnesses lie unconditionally in the positive rational binary subclass. The generic selection-equalizer lift instead supplies a positive rational finite witness in the published discrete class and lies in the positive rational binary subclass only when its base SCMs are binary. A countermodel pair in the binary subclass refutes identification in the larger class, but this negative transfer supplies no positive completeness implication. The equalizer's graph-membership conclusion applies only when the base pair has a common represented graph and the appended parent relations are active. The affine rank equivalence is conditional on a specified perturbation interval that remains in the represented class. The connected table proves nonvacuity and the same-graph perturbation proves that its lock is not structural. The implication from all reachable terminal failures to a represented residual forest with a locked rational pair, together with the advertised synthesis bound, remains exactly the graph-to-lock open question. Continuous variables, intervention inputs, faithfulness-only claims, and general finite-alphabet certificate completeness are outside scope.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(j\in\{0,1\}\). By the strict inequalities imposed on \(\lambda_c\) and the positivity of \(g_u(c)\),
\[
 0<\frac{\lambda_c}{g_u(c)}<1
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 0<1-\frac{\lambda_c}{g_u(c)}<1                         \tag{1}
\]
for every \(u\) and \(c\). Thus the displayed kernel for \(\mathcal S\), including its complementary probability for \(\mathcal S=0\), is strictly positive. The kernel for \(\mathcal C\) is strictly positive by hypothesis. All of its entries, and all entries of the \(\mathcal S\)-kernel, are rational. Since the base SCMs have finitely many states and positive rational local tables, adjoining these two binary kernels gives finite positive rational SCMs. Moreover, for any fixed \(u\), the normalization of \(g_u\) and the strict bounds on \(\lambda_c\) give
\[
 0<\Lambda=\lambda_0+\lambda_1
 <g_u(0)+g_u(1)=1.                                      \tag{2}
\]
In particular, every division by \(\Lambda\) below is legitimate.

Appending child vertices changes no old structural equation, and their private exogenous variables are independent of all old exogenous variables. Hence the marginal law of \(\mathcal W\) remains \(P_j\). If the \(\mathcal Y\)-component of \(w\) is \(u\), the SCM factorization, the common \(\mathcal C\)-kernel, and the common \(\mathcal S\)-kernel yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_j(\mathcal W=w,\mathcal C=c,\mathcal S=1)
 &=P_j(\mathcal W=w)
   P(\mathcal C=c\mid\mathcal Y=u)
   P(\mathcal S=1\mid\mathcal Y=u,\mathcal C=c)\\
 &=P_j(\mathcal W=w)g_u(c)\frac{\lambda_c}{g_u(c)}\\
 &=P_j(\mathcal W=w)\lambda_c.                           \tag{3}
\end{aligned}
\]
The cancellation in the last equality is valid because \(g_u(c)>0\). Summing (3) over the finitely many \(w\) and over \(c\in\{0,1\}\) gives
\[
 P_j(\mathcal S=1)=\sum_wP_j(\mathcal W=w)
                    \sum_{c=0}^1\lambda_c
                  =\Lambda.                              \tag{4}
\]
Equations (2)--(4) therefore imply
\[
 P_j(\mathcal W=w,\mathcal C=c\mid\mathcal S=1)
 =P_j(\mathcal W=w)\frac{\lambda_c}{\Lambda}.            \tag{5}
\]
The observational-equality premise says that the right-hand side of (5) is the same for \(j=0\) and \(j=1\). Thus the two full selected observational laws agree cell by cell.

Under \(\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x)\), SCM modularity replaces only the structural equations for \(\mathcal X\); it leaves both appended child kernels unchanged. Marginalizing the interventional analogue of (3) over the finitely many old coordinates other than \(\mathcal Y\) gives, for every outcome value \(u\),
\[
 P_j(\mathcal Y=u,\mathcal C=c,\mathcal S=1
      \mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x))
 =P_j(\mathcal Y=u\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x))
  \lambda_c.                                             \tag{6}
\]
Write \(p_j^x(u)=P_j(\mathcal Y=u\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x))\). Since \(\sum_u p_j^x(u)=1\), summing (6) first over \(u,c\) and then only over \(u\) proves, respectively,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_j(\mathcal S=1\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x))
   &=\sum_u p_j^x(u)\sum_{c=0}^1\lambda_c=\Lambda,\\
 P_j(\mathcal C=c,\mathcal S=1
      \mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x))
   &=\sum_u p_j^x(u)\lambda_c=\lambda_c.                 \tag{7}
\end{aligned}
\]
Dividing the second line of (7) by the first, using \(\Lambda>0\), yields the common positive conditioning denominator
\[
 D_j(c;x):=P_j(\mathcal C=c\mid
       \operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x),\mathcal S=1)
 =\frac{\lambda_c}{\Lambda}>0.                           \tag{8}
\]
Dividing (6) at \(u=y\) by the first line of (7) gives the selected joint numerator
\[
 N_j(y,c;x):=P_j(\mathcal Y=y,\mathcal C=c\mid
       \operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x),\mathcal S=1)
 =p_j^x(y)\frac{\lambda_c}{\Lambda}.                     \tag{9}
\]
The interventional-inequality premise gives \(p_0^x(y)\ne p_1^x(y)\). Since \(\lambda_c/\Lambda>0\), equation (9) implies \(N_0(y,c;x)\ne N_1(y,c;x)\), while (8) gives \(D_0(c;x)=D_1(c;x)\). Finally, division of (9) by (8), again justified by its strict positivity, gives
\[
 P_j(\mathcal Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x),
       \mathcal C=c,\mathcal S=1)
 =p_j^x(y).                                               \tag{10}
\]
Thus the selected conditional causal effects differ, even though the full selected observational laws and conditioning denominators coincide.

It remains to verify the conditional graph and support claims. Under the common-graph hypothesis, the two base graphs both equal \(\mathcal H\). The independent private exogenous variables introduce no latent common cause involving an old vertex, and the two new kernels name no old parent other than \(\mathcal Y\); consequently no edge other than the three displayed arrows is added. Nonconstancy of \(g_u(\cdot)\) in \(u\) makes \(\mathcal Y\) an active parent of \(\mathcal C\). It also supplies values \(u,u'\) and a value \(c\) for which \(g_u(c)\ne g_{u'}(c)\); because \(\lambda_c>0\),
\[
 \frac{\lambda_c}{g_u(c)}
 \ne
 \frac{\lambda_c}{g_{u'}(c)},                            \tag{11}
\]
so \(\mathcal Y\) is an active parent of \(\mathcal S\). The separate hypothesis that \(\lambda_c/g_u(c)\) is nonconstant in \(c\) for some fixed \(u\) makes \(\mathcal C\) an active parent of \(\mathcal S\). Hence both extensions have the common represented graph \(\mathcal H^+\) claimed in the statement.

If every endogenous variable in each base SCM is binary, the old variables remain binary and the two appended variables are binary by construction. Together with the positive rational table conclusion and the common represented graph just proved, this places the extensions in \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{rat,bin}}^+(\mathcal H^+)\). Without the binary-base premise, the same argument still places the finite positive rational extensions in \(\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal H^+)\) under the graph hypotheses, but it does not alter or encode any nonbinary base coordinate. Therefore it does not, by itself, produce a binary certificate pair \(\Gamma\).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Let \(\mathcal W\) be a finite observed vector containing a treatment subvector \(\mathcal X\) and a single finite outcome vertex \(\mathcal Y\). Let \(\mathbf Q_0\) and \(\mathbf Q_1\) be finite SCMs with positive rational local tables such that \(P_0(\mathcal W=w)=P_1(\mathcal W=w)\) for every observed cell \(w\), but, for some assignments \(x,y\),
\[
 P_0(\mathcal Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x))
 \ne
 P_1(\mathcal Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x)).
\]
Append binary vertices \(\mathcal C\) and \(\mathcal S\), driven by private exogenous variables independent of the old exogenous variables, and use the same new kernels in both SCMs. For rational numbers \(g_u(c)\) satisfying \(g_u(c)>0\) and \(\sum_{c=0}^1g_u(c)=1\) for every outcome value \(u\), choose rational \(\lambda_c\) such that
\[
 0<\lambda_c<\min_u g_u(c),
 \qquad c\in\{0,1\},
 \qquad
 \Lambda:=\lambda_0+\lambda_1,
\]
and set
\[
 P(\mathcal C=c\mid\mathcal Y=u)=g_u(c),
 \qquad
 P(\mathcal S=1\mid\mathcal Y=u,\mathcal C=c)
   =\frac{\lambda_c}{g_u(c)}.
\]
Then the two extended SCMs are finite, positive, and rational and, for \(j\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_j(\mathcal W=w,\mathcal C=c,\mathcal S=1)
   &=P_j(\mathcal W=w)\lambda_c,\\
 P_j(\mathcal S=1\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x))
   &=\Lambda,\\
 P_j(\mathcal C=c\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x),\mathcal S=1)
   &=\frac{\lambda_c}{\Lambda},\\
 P_j(\mathcal Y=y,\mathcal C=c\mid
       \operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x),\mathcal S=1)
   &=P_j(\mathcal Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x))
     \frac{\lambda_c}{\Lambda}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently the full selected observational laws and every positive conditioning denominator agree, whereas the displayed selected joint numerators and conditional causal effects disagree. Graph membership has the following conditional form only: if the two base SCMs have a common represented graph \(\mathcal H\), if \(g_u(\cdot)\) is nonconstant in \(u\), and if \(\lambda_c/g_u(c)\) is nonconstant in \(c\) for at least one fixed \(u\), then every proposed parent is active and both extensions have the common represented graph \(\mathcal H^+\) obtained from \(\mathcal H\) by adjoining \(\mathcal Y\to\mathcal C\), \(\mathcal Y\to\mathcal S\), and \(\mathcal C\to\mathcal S\). If the base SCMs are binary, the extensions lie in \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{rat,bin}}^+(\mathcal H^+)\). Otherwise the lemma supplies a positive rational finite witness in the published discrete class \(\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal H^+)\), under the stated graph-membership hypotheses, but does not supply a binary certificate pair \(\Gamma\) without a further encoding argument.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The requested scope repair retains the finite-base result while making binary-certificate membership conditional on binary base SCMs; no encoding of nonbinary base coordinates is proved.
